answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it votes on jobs or earns rewards. A glacier-paced withdrawal delay lets peers challenge suspicious clusters; if linked accounts coordinate to claim the same work or recycle payments, an audit can slash their bonds and exclude them. The stake need not prove a unique human, but it makes each Sybil costly: an attacker must tie up capital per identity and risks losing it. Timber and dune can label ordinary jobs, not bypass that cost.
